title: Sickness or injury? Definition decides when IP benefits end
full_text:
Sickness or injury? Definition decides when IP benefits end
A claimant who wanted his sickness characterised as a psychological injury so he could continue to receive income protection benefits has lost a dispute before the financial services ombudsman.
The man’s mental ill health is a sickness under the policy because it is not an accidental bodily injury, the Australian Financial Complaints Authority says.
AFCA notes the Resolution Life policy stops income protection benefits at age 65, “but if his condition is characterised as an injury, his IP benefits are payable for life”.
The man made a successful IP claim in March 2015 after suffering anxiety and depression following workplace bullying and harassment.
A workers’ compensation claim against his employer was accepted in August 2015 on the basis he had suffered a psychological injury.
When he made a successful TPD claim in March 2016, Resolution treated his illness as a sickness.
In 2024, the man turned 65 and Resolution told him the IP benefits would end in August 2025.
Before 2024, there was nothing to suggest his condition was an injury, the ombudsman says.
A treating psychiatrist wrote in 2024 and 2025 that the man suffered a psychological injury leading to his anxiety and depression in 2014, but the ombudsman says medical evidence closer to 2014 supports the cause of total disablement being a sickness.
“It is not fair to expect the insurer to retrospectively recharacterise the basis for the complainant’s claim, particularly based on recent theoretical medical opinion. Unless the complainant’s condition is an accidental bodily injury, the insurer must treat it as a sickness.”
